headline_marked: Actress Badhan assaulted in Venice; [[Mousumi Hamid condemns attack]], calls being an artist 'a sin'
headline: Actress Badhan assaulted in Venice; Mousumi Hamid condemns attack, calls being an artist 'a sin'
summary: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan was reportedly assaulted and harassed in Venice, Italy. Fellow actress Mousumi Hamid voiced outrage on Facebook, stating that in Bangladesh, being an artist feels like a sin.
details: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan, who was in Venice, Italy, to represent Bangladeshi cinema, has reportedly been assaulted and harassed. The incident has drawn widespread condemnation from the Bangladeshi entertainment community.

Fellow actress Mousumi Hamid took to Facebook to express her strong disapproval of the attack. She stated that such incidents make it feel like being an artist in Bangladesh is a sin, as artists often find themselves speaking out on political issues.

Hamid emphasized that no artist should face such attacks, whether in Bangladesh or abroad. She criticized those who downplay the incident by comparing it to past events, suggesting that such comparisons justify further aggression.

She further argued that leaders should strive to unite people, like historical figures such as Bangabandhu, Ziaur Rahman, and Maulana Bhashani, rather than dividing them based on political affiliation. Hamid lamented that society is increasingly judging individuals by their political leanings rather than their humanity.
caption:
Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan assaulted in Venice.
Fellow artist Mousumi Hamid says, 'In Bangladesh, being an artist feels like a sin.'

Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan, who was in Venice, Italy, to represent Bangladeshi cinema, has reportedly been assaulted and harassed. The incident has drawn widespread condemnation from the Bangladeshi entertainment community.

Fellow actress Mousumi Hamid took to Facebook to express her strong disapproval of the attack. She stated that such incidents make it feel like being an artist in Bangladesh is a sin, as artists often find themselves speaking out on political issues.

Hamid emphasized that no artist should face such attacks, whether in Bangladesh or abroad. She criticized those who downplay the incident by comparing it to past events, suggesting that such comparisons justify further aggression.

She further argued that leaders should strive to unite people, like historical figures such as Bangabandhu, Ziaur Rahman, and Maulana Bhashani, rather than dividing them based on political affiliation. Hamid lamented that society is increasingly judging individuals by their political leanings rather than their humanity.

headline_marked: Govt to launch [[3-month special campaign to prevent dengue]] starting Saturday
headline: Govt to launch 3-month special campaign to prevent dengue starting Saturday
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed a nationwide drive focusing on cleanliness and public awareness to combat the mosquito-borne disease.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for active public participation in a special three-month campaign to prevent dengue, identifying the next three months as a high-risk period.
The campaign, which officially begins this Saturday, September 12, will focus on cleaning and public awareness initiatives to reduce mosquito breeding sites.
The Prime Minister emphasized that dengue control should not rely solely on mosquito eradication efforts but must prioritize cleanliness and public awareness.
The drive will involve local administrations, voluntary organizations, and students from schools and colleges to ensure coordinated field-level activities.
City corporations in metropolitan areas and Deputy Commissioners at the district level will coordinate the activities, while Upazila Nirbahi Officers (UNOs) will lead at the উপজেলা (upazila) level.
Volunteers from the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief, Scouts, BNCC, Girl Guides, and the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society will be actively involved in the campaign.
Every Saturday, volunteers and students will visit homes and establishments to assist with cleaning and identifying mosquito breeding grounds.
The government will also launch a wide-scale awareness campaign via mass media and social media, including regular television broadcasts and social media messages to educate the public.
caption:
The government is launching a nationwide 3-month drive to fight dengue. Cleanliness and public awareness are now the priority.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for active public participation in a special three-month campaign to prevent dengue, identifying the next three months as a high-risk period.

The campaign, which officially begins this Saturday, September 12, will focus on cleaning and public awareness initiatives to reduce mosquito breeding sites.

The Prime Minister emphasized that dengue control should not rely solely on mosquito eradication efforts but must prioritize cleanliness and public awareness.

The drive will involve local administrations, voluntary organizations, and students from schools and colleges to ensure coordinated field-level activities.

City corporations in metropolitan areas and Deputy Commissioners at the district level will coordinate the activities, while Upazila Nirbahi Officers (UNOs) will lead at the উপজেলা (upazila) level.

Volunteers from the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief, Scouts, BNCC, Girl Guides, and the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society will be actively involved in the campaign.

Every Saturday, volunteers and students will visit homes and establishments to assist with cleaning and identifying mosquito breeding grounds.

The government will also launch a wide-scale awareness campaign via mass media and social media, including regular television broadcasts and social media messages to educate the public.
